text: Basic effects: the batteries that come with doeff.
Each one is an effect your code yields, and a handler that ships with doeff answers it.
Reader. Ask, with a key, reads a value from the environment.
The environment lives in the reader handler. Your code only names the key it wants.
A key that is not there raises a missing env key error, and the message names the close key.
Next, with_custom_config runs fetch_data with a staging URL.
First, Ask reads api_url, and Tell logs the default.
Then Local runs fetch_data over a changed environment.
Inside, Ask sees the override. The code of fetch_data is the same as ever.
When Local returns, Ask reads the default URL again.
State. Get and Put read and write a store.
The store lives in the state handler, not in your code.
Get, add one, Put, three times over. The program returns three.
Writer. Tell appends a message to a log.
A handler can perform effects too. Writer keeps its log in state, with its own Get and Put.
ReadWriterLog reads the log back: four lines, in the order they were told.
slog emits a structured entry: a message, plus keyword data.
slog handler prints each entry on standard error. It is a separate effect from Tell.
Listen collects the entries as values, so a test can check them.
Now put them together. application_workflow retries an operation and logs each try.
It reads max_retries, logs it, and sets attempt to zero.
Each round, it counts and logs the attempt, then tries.
On success it returns. Otherwise it logs the failure, and goes round again.
Stack three handlers around it: reader, state, and writer.
Each effect goes out to the layer that handles it. Ask to reader, Tell to writer, Put and Get to state.
The second attempt succeeds. The log holds every step, and the result is success.
Reader, State, Writer, and slog: effects your code yields, and handlers that come with doeff, stacked the way your program needs.
